faqs.q: What should I include on a Christmas light installation estimate?
faqs.a: At minimum: your business name, the client and job-site address, a dated line-item list (roofline lighting by the linear foot, wreaths, garland, timers, takedown, labor), a validity date, deposit terms, and a note that it is not a final invoice.

faqs.q: How much does Christmas light installation cost?
faqs.a: Most US companies charge $8–$12 per linear foot of roofline lighting with materials and labor included, so a 150 ft single-story roofline runs $1,350–$1,800 for the season. Wreaths and garland run $30–$60 per piece, timers $25–$50, and takedown is often bundled into the per-foot rate.

faqs.q: How much deposit should I collect?
faqs.a: 50% is the industry standard for holiday lighting — it covers the lights and materials you buy before install day. The balance is due once the display is up and the client has signed off.

faqs.q: Is this template free to use?
faqs.a: Yes. All three formats (PDF, Word, Excel) are free to download with no email required.

faqs.q: Does the Excel version calculate the deposit automatically?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter your quantities and rates, and the subtotal, 50% deposit and balance due update automatically.

faqs.q: Is this legal or tax advice?
faqs.a: No. Templates are for informational purposes only. Requirements vary by state — verify with your contractor board and a CPA or attorney before use.
